about: What calls on the runtime conformance plugin (conformance-weather) return: one list that both the real runtimes and the SDK testing tools are checked against (issue #206, risk A1, Q6.7.2).

Real runtimes: rutis_bridge::runtime::testing::runtime (crates/rutis-bridge/tests/session_matrix.rs). Testing tools: node/rutis/test/conformance.test.mjs (@arcships/rutis/testing), in strict mode, go/rutis/rutistest/conformance_test.go (rutistest), kotlin/rutis/rutis-conformance/src/test/kotlin/arcships/rutis/conformance/WeatherConformanceTest.kt (arcships.rutis.testing) and swift/rutis/Tests/RutisTests/WeatherConformanceTests.swift (RutisTest).
The plugin injects `clock`, whose `now()` returns 0, 1, 2, ... one per call, and provides `service` with `methods`.

A call: `call` (method), `args` (JSON; {"$callback": ...} is a function the caller passes: "upper" returns its argument upper-cased; {"throws": {name, message, fields}} throws an error with that name and message and extra `fields`), and what it does: `returns` (a JSON value; keys in `ignore` are not compared; `copied`: it is not the object passed in), `throws` ({} for any error, or the `name` and `message` the caller receives; the thrown error's extra `fields` do not cross) or `exits` (the plugin's process exits with this status).
`samples` are values one language makes: the plugin's `samples()` names the ones it has, `sample(name)` returns one; a runtime whose plugin has no `samples` method has none.

`events` (after `calls` and `samples`): the host emits `emit` with `args` (JSON) with `parallel` on its bus, which the runtime's listeners joined (docs/design-events-protocol-2026-10-18.md); then `then` is a call as in `calls`, or the emission `throws`. The session matrix requires these checks on Node, Bun, Python, Go and Swift; the testing tools emit the same in one process.
`allowed`: the testing tool does not do what this entry says, and why (a bounded, written-down difference, also in docs/guide/plugin-api.md). Every other entry holds for both.

Tagged values (#308, docs/design-value-types-2026-10-15.md) are written {"$<tag>": <the value's wire text>}: {"$instant": "2026-10-15T03:22:15.123Z"}, {"$bytes": "aGVsbG8="} (base64), {"$map": [[key, value], ...]}, {"$set": [element, ...]}, and so for datetime, date, time, bigint, decimal and uuid. No plain value is written so.

`pending`: no runtime's plugin names this sample yet; a runtime names it in its `samples()` once it sends that value (#308 phase 3), and the entry then holds for it like any other. Until then it is not checked.

`undeclared` (#442): the plugin also provides `service` without declaring it in `provides`. rutis sees `methods`, the methods inferred from the object (JavaScript: its own and inherited functions, not `constructor`; Python: its public callables; Go: its exported methods), every one `async`; its fields are not methods. Then `calls`, as above. A runtime announces it to a host that asks (rows.announce); a testing tool shows it the same way.

calls.why: a sync call that calls a host service
the host service is called on every call
a callback during a sync call
an error crosses twice (callback to plugin, plugin to caller) with its name and message, not as the object thrown
data crosses both ways as a copy

calls.allowed: the testing tool runs the plugin in the test's own process, so a plugin that ends its process ends the test: the tool cannot show this, and tests do not call it

calls.why: a service the plugin provides without declaring it is used by name, its method called async
an inherited method (a prototype's in JavaScript, a base class's in Python, an embedded type's in Go) is one of its methods

events.why: a leaf listener hears a host event without declaring anything, and the host's parallel waits for it: its effect is visible to the next call

samples.why: a number that is not finite does not cross
undefined inside data arrives as null
an Error returned as a value arrives as data: its name, message and stack
a tuple arrives as a list
a dataclass arrives as a dict
a set arrives as a set (#308)
bytes arrive as bytes (#308)
a float that is not finite does not cross
a dict with keys that are not strings arrives as a map (#308)
an exception returned as a value arrives as data: its name and message
integers within ±(2^53−1) cross, and a bool stays a bool
an int beyond ±(2^53−1) arrives as a big integer, with no wrapper (design V6): as a number, past 2^64 Rust would read it as a float, past 2^53 JavaScript cannot hold it exactly (#356)
so does one inside data, the data around it kept
a Date (new Date('2026-10-15T03:22:15.123Z')) arrives as an instant
a Uint8Array arrives as bytes
a Map arrives as a map, its keys of different kinds kept apart and in order, undefined as null
a Set arrives as a set, in order
a bigint arrives as a big integer
the SDK constructors send a datetime, date, time, decimal and uuid; the decimal keeps its trailing zero
a Map keyed by a Date does not cross: a Date compares by identity as a key (design §5)
an invalid Date does not cross: it names no instant
a map key that is an integer beyond ±(2^53−1) does not cross: send it as a bigint (design V6, §5)
a Set whose elements are equal values (two rutis.date('2026-10-15')) does not cross: a language that merges them would lose one (design §5)
a typed array other than Uint8Array (an Int16Array) does not cross as bytes: its element type would be lost
undefined inside data arrives as null: a dict keeps the key (#355, design V10)
a datetime with a time zone (here +02:00) arrives as an instant in UTC, to the microsecond
a datetime without a time zone arrives as a local datetime, not read in any zone (design V5)
a Decimal (its trailing zeros kept) and a UUID (in lowercase) arrive as values, not as object references (#355)
a dict with integer keys arrives as a map, in order
a date and a time without a time zone arrive as a date and a time of day
a plain int beyond ±(2^53−1) arrives as a big integer (design V6)
a dict with a key that is not a string arrives as a map, its string keys too, in order; a frozenset as a set
a bytearray and a memoryview arrive as bytes
a time with a time zone does not cross: a time of day has none (design §6)
a Decimal that is not finite does not cross
a dict keyed by a tuple does not cross: a map key is a string, number, boolean, bigint, datetime, date, time, decimal or uuid (design §5)
a time.Time arrives as an instant in UTC, to the nanosecond
a []byte inside a struct arrives as bytes, not as base64 text (V9)
a time.Time inside a struct (here at +02:00) arrives as an instant in UTC, not as RFC 3339 text in its zone (V9)
a map with integer keys arrives as a map, its keys in order
a map[K]struct{} arrives as a set, its elements in order
a *big.Int arrives as a big integer
advanced.DateTime, Date, TimeOfDay, Decimal and UUID arrive as a datetime, date, time, decimal and uuid; the decimal keeps its trailing zero
an int64 beyond ±(2^53−1), here inside a struct, arrives as a big integer (V6, V9): no *big.Int needed
map keys beyond ±(2^53−1) arrive as big integers, the others as numbers (V6)
a Date arrives as an instant in UTC, to the microsecond (a Date holds about that much)
inside a Codable struct a Data arrives as bytes, a Date as an instant and an Int64 beyond ±(2^53−1) as a big integer, not as JSONEncoder's base64, number or plain number (V9, V6)
a Dictionary with Int keys arrives as a map, its keys in order (a Dictionary has no order of its own: numbers by value)
a Set arrives as a set, its elements in order
a Rutis.Advanced.BigInt arrives as a big integer
a UInt64 beyond ±(2^53−1) arrives as a big integer, with no wrapper (V6)
Rutis.Advanced.DateTime, CalendarDate and TimeOfDay, a Decimal and a UUID (in lowercase) arrive as a datetime, date, time, decimal and uuid
a Double that is not finite does not cross
a Dictionary keyed by Date does not cross: a point in time is no map key (design §5)
an Error returned as a value arrives as data: its name (its type's) and message (its errorDescription)
a java.time.Instant (made from 05:22:15.123456789+02:00) arrives as an instant in UTC, to the nanosecond
kotlin.time.Instant and kotlin.uuid.Uuid arrive as an instant and a uuid, as their java counterparts
a ByteArray and an Instant inside a @Serializable class arrive as bytes and an instant, not as a list of numbers or text (RutisFormat, never JSON's default encoding)
a Map with Int keys arrives as a map, its keys in order
a Set arrives as a set, its elements in order
a BigInteger arrives as a big integer
LocalDateTime, LocalDate, LocalTime, BigDecimal and UUID arrive as a datetime, date, time, decimal and uuid; the decimal keeps its trailing zero (its scale)
a Long beyond ±(2^53−1), here inside a @Serializable class, arrives as a big integer (V6): no BigInteger needed
map keys beyond ±(2^53−1) arrive as big integers, the others as numbers (V6)
a Double that is not finite does not cross
an exception returned as a value arrives as data: its name and message
